title: Moss and the Web
checkpoint: Reception Autumn 2, week 4 — Learning — Phase 3: new sounds j, v, w
note_for_grown_ups: The very first Phase 3 sounds (j, v, w) are taught here — this is also the first book with 8 pages instead of 7, matching the slightly longer books from this point on.

pages.text: Moss got up. It is wet.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog waking up under a hedge on a damp grey morning, raindrops on the leaves.

pages.text: A web is on a red van.
pages.illustration: A small red toy van left in the grass, a round spider web strung across its front, beaded with raindrops.

pages.text: Will Moss get on the van?
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog looking up at the red toy van and its web, one paw raised.

pages.text: No! Moss will not rip the web.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog stepping back from the red toy van so the web stays whole.

pages.text: Moss sat on a jug. Moss sat and sat.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog sitting on an upturned blue jug in the grass, waiting patiently beside the red toy van.

pages.text: The sun got up. The web is not wet.
pages.illustration: Warm sunshine on the garden, the web on the red toy van now dry and shining.

pages.text: A bug is on the web!
pages.illustration: A small black beetle walking on the dry web on the red toy van, Moss watching from the blue jug.

pages.text: Moss did not rip the web. Moss did well.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog trotting off across the sunny grass, the web on the red toy van still whole behind him.
